analysis:
The supplied files are documentation only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md and docs/architecture/inference.md. No executable code, key handling, attestation, WebSocket, cache-storage or authorization code is modified, so I found no concrete security regression.

hardware-support.md changes (head lines 102-108, 177-215, 317-325, 432-439): documents local HTTP Responses host-side JSON retention, GLM sparse KV sizing and load admission, MiMo prompt recount, and MTP request-generation binding. The retention note (102-108) says the SDK response-object store has no matching eviction. It describes application memory and a possible availability or memory-pressure concern, which is relevant to T-010 and T-029. It is documentation of existing behavior, not a new change in this PR. It also contains a possible data-at-rest and in-memory plaintext retention aspect for A-001 (consumer prompts). Whether that store is reachable by coordinator-routed traffic or only by local direct-mode HTTP is not established by the supplied text, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.

inference.md: only the patch excerpt and the range map are supplied, and no base or head text unit is available for 9bceb6d953b336e2:0. The excerpt notes that a refused SSD store's typed reason reaches the bridge for local /metrics only. This touches T-041 (the prefix-cache oracle). The leak surface would depend on whether /metrics is local-only and whether the reason strings expose prefix or tenant data. That cannot be verified from the supplied evidence. I recommend the next pass check the inference.md head ranges 617-856, 1457-1514 and 1797-1822 for claims that diverge from T-041 (the 30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup names, and no persistent RAM carve) or from the TB-011 and T-053 authorization wording. The metrics-reason exposure should also be checked against the actual code.

No threat-model assumptions appear to be invalidated by the supplied text. The remaining uncertainty is limited to the unseen inference.md content.
